maria_eng: Quick question — trying to lock down the precedence rules for flags before I open a PR. Current mental model: org > project > route > model, but with exception that certain guardrail flags (eg rate_limit, deny_exports) must be enforced org-wide and cannot be relaxed downstream. Is that the right rule?

sam_platform: Yep that matches what we discussed. Practical shorthand: default at org, allow narrowing (more restrictive) at project/route/model, but model cannot escalate above org. So precedence for value resolution is model -> route -> project -> org (closest wins), but enforcement-level flags are always evaluated at org first and short-circuit.

maria_eng: Nice — can you check this snippet for the config semantics? thinking to put in docs and test matrix.

sam_platform: ````yaml
flags:
  org_defaults:
    allow_tool_calls: true     # can be overridden lower-level
    rate_limit: 1000          # guardrail: cannot be raised below org min
  projects:
    team-alpha:
      routes:
        /generate:
          flags:
            allow_tool_calls: false
            model_overrides:
              gpt-x-1: { allow_tool_calls: true }  # model-level can re-enable, but check guardrail
````

chloe_pm: One nuance from product: if model_overrides tries to set `rate_limit` higher than org_min we should reject at validation time. We don't want silent misconfig where model thinks it has higher quota. Also if route sets a canary audience, that should be independent — route can narrow to `team:beta` even if org has broader canary.

terry_sre: Agree with both. Operationally: add a validation rule: if flag is marked `org_enforced: true` then any lower-level config that attempts `>` or `=` on that metric -> fail PR CI. Also add a runtime check to log violations and fallback to org value. Prevents canary leakage.

maria_eng: Good call. I'll add CI lint and runtime fallback logging. Quick ask: where should the docs live? eng-platform or docs repo?

sam_platform: Put a short explainer + table in eng-platform so infra folks see it; link to longer spec in docs repo. Also add testcases in flags-service unit tests for: (a) model override of non-enforced flag, (b) attempted model escalate of enforced flag -> CI fail, (c) route-level canary isolation.

chloe_pm: For rollout UX, ensure Console shows "effective value" and top-line origin (org/project/route/model) so PMs can see why a value is in effect.

deploy-bot: Deploy preview created: https://deploys.redwood.ai/previews/flag-precedence-1865129999 — PR #4217

maria_eng: OK I'll open PR with docs + lint rule + 3 unit tests, pinging @sam_platform and @terry_sre for review. Thanks all :thumbsup:

sam_platform: Thanks — leave a TODO to add an e2e scenario where route canary users actually get routed vs control group.

terry_sre: Also add a quick runbook note: how to rollback if a model-level override accidentally enables a restricted feature.

maria_eng: noted, will include runbook snippet in PR."
